meta.what: Military support to Russia from foreign states (weapons, ammunition, troops, intelligence) not already in recorded trade, round 6 revision of flowback2.json military_to_russia.
meta.units: EUR bn nominal; 2026 = Jan-Aug, not annualised. USD converted with ECB yearly averages 2022 1.053, 2023 1.081, 2024 1.082, 2025 1.13, 2026 1.16.
meta.method: Quantity x market value (what Russia pays its own industry or paid the supplier), per item and year; low/central/high are ~90% ranges; country totals = sum of item lows/centrals/highs (fully correlated). Always toward Russia. Counted in full (support, mostly paid in kind), not at profit, because none of it is in customs data. Direct replacement for flowback2.json military_to_russia (same keys: total_eur_bn, by_year, items, sources, belligerent_sources_flag, reasoning; plus certainty and by_item_eur_bn).

items.artillery_ammunition: 152mm-equivalent rounds incl. 122mm and Grad rockets: low 6.5m (HUR), central 10m (OSC 8-11m to Jan 2026 + small 2026), high 15m (ROK DIA, 33,000 containers). Valued at what Russia pays its own industry for a 152mm round (USD 1,000-1,300, procurement data) with a quality discount (about half outdated, many 122mm and mortar rounds): USD 400 / 800 / 1,100 per round. Shipment timing from container counts and HUR (2025 about half of 2024 by HUR, but OSC counts show a steady 2025): 17% 2023, 42% 2024, 38% 2025, 3% Jan-Aug 2026 (two ships noted Jan-Mar 2026).
items.ballistic_missiles: KN-23/24: 150 / 220 / 280 (MSMT >=100 in 2024; INSS ~250 by early 2026) at USD 1.5m / 2.5m / 3.5m (Iskander-class).
items.artillery_systems: 220 pieces (ROK DIA: Koksan 170mm SPGs, 240mm MLRS) at USD 0.5m / 1m / 2m each.
items.troops: INSS: USD 0.62bn Oct 2024-Dec 2025 (pay USD 2,800-5,000/month, death benefits), ~USD 0.56bn/yr if continued -> Jan-Aug 2026 USD 0.37bn. Range 0.7x-1.5x (other reports USD 2,000/month; 2026 rotations of engineers/deminers).
items.workers: 15,000-25,000 labourers in Russia: NOT valued (paid wages, labour market transaction).

sources.name: NK News on INSS (Seoul): North Korea's revenue from military cooperation with Russia USD 7.7-14.4bn Aug 2023-Dec 2025 (artillery etc. USD 7.05-13.78bn; troops USD 0.62bn Oct 2024-Dec 2025; pay USD 2,800-5,000/month; ~USD 560m/yr if continued)
Bloomberg on INSS: North Korea gave Russia up to USD 14bn; 80-96% of compensation in military technology and components
IStories with Open Source Centre: at least 29,488 containers Sep 2023-Jan 2026 = 8-11m shells and rockets; Rajin to Tikhoretsk
Korea Times: ROK Defense Intelligence Agency - about 33,000 containers of weapons to Russia (28,000 in Jul 2025); 220 artillery pieces
Kyiv Independent: ROK DIA - >28,000 containers, >12m 152mm-equivalent rounds
Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team report MSMT 2025-1 (via Ukrainska Pravda): up to 9m artillery and rocket rounds and at least 100 ballistic missiles in 2024; >200 pieces of equipment
Pryamiy on Reuters: HUR deputy head Skibitsky - ~6.5m shells since 2023; 2025 deliveries half of 2024; about half outdated (BELLIGERENT)
Maritime Executive: North Korean shipments of shells to Russia tail off (two shipments noted Jan-Mar 2026)
Hromadske on Nikkei/INSS: ~USD 13bn in three years; ~250 KN-23; >USD 600m for troops; ~USD 2,000/month per soldier
Conflict Armament Research: Documenting a North Korean missile in Ukraine (KN-23/24 in Kharkiv, Jan 2024)
Euromaidan Press on Militarnyi (Russian state procurement): standard 152mm round ~USD 1,200 in 2024, >USD 1,300 in 2025
Militarnyi on Sky News/Bain: Russian 152mm shell ~USD 1,000 vs NATO 155mm ~USD 4,000

PRK.belligerent_sources_flag: Only the low shell count (6.5m) is Ukrainian HUR. Central and high rest on OSC (independent UK NGO), MSMT (11-state monitoring team), ROK DIA and INSS (South Korean state). Prices from Russian procurement records (published by a Ukrainian outlet).
PRK.payment_note: INSS: 80-96% of Russia's compensation is military technology and components, cash only 4-20%. Valued here at market value (what Russia would pay), as the method asks; the cash actually received by Pyongyang is much smaller.
PRK.reasoning: Raised from D to C: several independent quantity sources (OSC container counts, ROK DIA, MSMT, HUR) now agree within a factor of ~2, the INSS valuation exists, and prices can be pinned to Russia's own procurement prices. Central EUR 8.8bn (2022-Aug 2026); to Dec 2025 EUR 8.3bn vs INSS EUR 6.9-13.0bn. Replaces flowback2 military_to_russia.PRK AND narrow.json PRK.military_rus (central 10.85, which had 2025 > 2024 and kept 2026 at EUR 1bn, now EUR 0.58bn given the 2026 slowdown).

items.drones_direct_2022_23: Shahed-136/131 and Mohajer-6 shipped ready-made Aug 2022-mid 2023: 1,000 / 1,700 / 2,400 (ISIS: ~1,100 launched before Alabuga output; 2,400 reported agreed) at USD 50k / 150k / 290k (leaked negotiation prices USD 193-290k; Iranian cost far lower).
items.alabuga_contract_drones_licence: Leaked contract USD 1.75bn (108.5bn RUB) early 2023: technology transfer, equipment, 6,000 kits, licence, software. Low USD 1.0bn (programme cost 'just under USD 1bn' in the same files; only ~2 t gold = ~USD 0.13bn of payment seen). High USD 2.05bn adds components after 2024. Paid 2023 50% / 2024 35% / 2025 15%. Russia's own Geran output after localisation is NOT Iranian supply and is not counted.
items.missiles_ballistic_and_sam: Bloomberg: contracts ~USD 2.7bn (hundreds of Fath-360, ~500 other SRBMs, ~200 SAMs); Cavoli: >400 SRBMs delivered; Fath-360 delivery confirmed Sep 2024 but use in Ukraine not seen. Low USD 0.45bn (400 SRBM x USD 1m + some SAMs), central USD 1.6bn (~60% of contract delivered), high USD 2.7bn (full contract).
items.ammunition: WSJ: 300,000 shells and 1m rounds (2023); 'millions of rounds' later. 300k x USD 400 to 500k x USD 1,000 plus small arms.

su35_netting.note: Russia's Su-35 sale to Iran (48 aircraft, ~EUR 6bn, delivered from 2026; russian_arms_exports.json) may be partly paid with these drones/missiles. If so, net: the part of the amounts below that settled the Su-35 must not count both as Iran's payment for arms AND as Iran's supply to Russia. Iranian supply to Russia that could be barter (drones + missiles + ammo), EUR bn central:

sources.name: Militarnyi on Bloomberg: Iranian missile contracts ~USD 2.7bn since Oct 2021 (hundreds of Fath-360, ~500 other SRBMs, ~200 SAMs); Shahed contract USD 1.75bn; total >USD 4bn
RFE/RL: Cavoli - Iran delivered over 400 SRBMs; Pentagon confirmed Fath-360 delivery Sep 2024; WSJ 300,000 shells and 1m rounds (2023); ~90% of Geran cycle now in Russia

The War Zone: What does a Shahed-136 really cost? Leaked Alabuga files - asked USD 375k, agreed USD 193k (6,000 units) or 290k (2,000); localisation transfer price USD 165.5k; >2 t gold paid (unverified)
LB.ua: hackers leak cost of Iranian Shaheds; 2,067,795 g gold from Alabuga to Sahara Thunder (Feb 2023)
Institute for Science and International Security: Alabuga production rate - ~1,100 Shaheds launched before Alabuga output; Iran delivered 600 kits; Alabuga >=2,300 airframes Apr-Dec 2023
FDD Long War Journal: Russia ships TNT, ammunition and drone components to Iran (flow reversed, Jul-Aug 2026)

IRN.belligerent_sources_flag: Contract values from an anonymous Western official (Bloomberg) and hacked Iranian files (authenticity unconfirmed); drone counts from Ukrainian Air Force data via ISIS (US NGO).
IRN.reasoning: Raised to C: contract values from two separate sources (leaked contract, Bloomberg official) and a US commander's delivered count. Central EUR 3.5bn (was 4.3): lower because contracts are not all deliveries and Russia's own Geran production is not Iranian supply. 2026 = 0: since the 2025-26 Iran war the flow has reversed (Russia ships TNT, ammunition and drone parts to Iran, Jul-Aug 2026).

items.ammunition_from_stocks: From the Belarusian army's stocks (not trade): 131.6 kt Jan 2022-Feb 2023, ~4.5-5 kt in 2024 (192 railcars), loading of Russian wagons at Belarusian depots in Sep 2025. Total 140 / 160 / 190 kt at USD 4,000 / 8,000 / 14,000 per tonne (a packed 152mm round ~80 kg at USD 700-1,100 is ~USD 9-13k/t; old stock, mixed with small arms and some SAMs).
items.armour_from_storage: T-72A and other vehicles from storage: 94 / 110 / 130 at USD 0.2m / 0.4m / 0.6m.
items.production_outside_trade: 'Uchastok' state ammunition project (hull plant from mid-2026, ~120,000/yr capacity): 2026 USD 0 / 0.03 / 0.15bn.
items.in_trade_not_counted: Components from Belarusian companies (Peleng sights, MZKT chassis, Grad rocket parts, Integral chips; BIC: >USD 1.2bn Feb 2022-Aug 2025, doubling 2022-2024) are commercial sales inside Belarus's exports to Russia (narrow.json BLR to_rus, pinned by official totals): NOT added here. Aircraft and air-defence repairs for Russia (558th ARZ, Monitor Service) are services, inside the reported rise in Belarus-Russia services trade: NOT added.

sources.name: Ukrainska Pravda / Belarusian railway workers: 131,500 t ammunition to Russia in one year (Jan 2022-Feb 2023)

Militarnyi: Role of the defence industry of Belarus (Prism UA): >130,000 t from stocks 2022-23; 2024 192 railcars ~4,500-5,000 t; Russia 26% (2019) to 60% (2022) of Belarusian defence exports; Grad parts 13,000 sets/month; filling line ~180,000 shells/yr
OCCRP / Belarusian Investigative Center: 58 Belarusian firms shipped >USD 1.2bn of components to 41 Russian arms makers Feb 2022-Aug 2025 (export data)
Euromaidan Press (BelPol): 'Uchastok' full-cycle 122/152mm ammunition plant for Russia by end-2026, hull plant ~120,000/yr from mid-2026
iSANS Belarus Review: empty Russian wagons sent to Belarusian depots to load ammunition for Russia (Sep 2025)

BLR.belligerent_sources_flag: Quantities from Belarusian opposition and activist groups (railway workers, Hajun, BelPol) and Prism UA; no official valuation. Prices are my valuation.
BLR.reasoning: Kept at D: quantities are activist counts, prices are mine (raised from USD 3-12k/t to 4-14k/t to match Russia's own procurement prices). Central EUR 1.27bn (was 1.2), 73% in 2022. Payment terms unknown (Belarus depends on Russian credit and energy subsidies).

items.uncounted_only: Identical to china_military.json items.uncounted_total (unrecorded finished military items 15% of their value, smuggled dual-use goods, satellite intelligence/training). Recorded dual-use exports (EUR 4.5-5.8bn/yr) are in China's customs exports to Russia: display only, never add.

sources.name: china_military.json (round 5) and its notes

CHN.reasoning: No new evidence found in this round that changes china_military.json; repeated here so the series sits in one place. The builder already uses china_military.json for CHN; use one of the two, not both (identical numbers).

MMR.note: Tank sights and cameras bought back by Uralvagonzavod from Myanmar's army (USD 24m, late 2022, Nikkei from Russian customs records). Already in customs trade and tiny: not added.

IND.note: USD 0.15m missile sight parts bought back by NPK KBM (customs records). Not added.

SYR.note: No evidence of Syrian arms transfers to Russia 2022-2024 (Syria was a recipient; Russia withdrew its own S-300 and personnel from Syria, which is not Syrian support). Nothing counted.

ERI.note: Political support only (UN votes); no material military supplies found. Nothing counted.

minor_suppliers.other: Foreign fighters (Central Asia, Africa, South Asia, Cuba, Nepal) are individual recruits paid by Russia: counts only, in flowback2.fighters_for_russia, not money.

overlaps: 1) Replaces flowback2.json military_to_russia (all four countries) AND narrow.json countries.PRK.military_rus (apply_narrow currently overwrites PRK after the military section; it must not). 2) CHN equals china_military.json uncounted_total: use one. 3) Belarus: only army-stock transfers, armour and non-trade state production; company components (BIC >USD 1.2bn) and repairs are inside Belarus's goods/services exports to Russia and are not added. 4) China's recorded dual-use goods stay in trade. 5) Iran: possible barter for Su-35s in russian_arms_exports.json, see countries.IRN.su35_netting. 6) Myanmar/India buy-backs are in customs (not added). 7) North Korean workers' wages not valued (labour). 8) Russia's own Geran production at Alabuga is not counted as Iranian supply.
